text.p: Pakistan hopes to privatise state-run Karachi Electric Supply Corp (KESC) by September, its managing director Shahid Hamid said on Thursday.
He told a news conference the government had already appointed financial advisers who were due to report by the end of January on how the privatisation would take place.

Hamid said it had not yet been decided whether to follow the strategy adopted for other major privatisations in Pakistan and sell a 26 percent stake in KESC to a strategic investor who would take over management control.
He said the KESC's liabilities included foreign loans worth 9.5 billion rupees, local loans totalling 7.2 billion rupees and 4.8 billion rupees raised in self-finance scheme loans.
The KESC's 10-rupee share closed unchanged at 18.50 rupees on Thursday at the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE)
One stock broker said the firm, set up in 1913, had a listed paid-up capital of 1.782 billion rupees on the KSE, but its assets and land were worth several billion dollars.
KESC's board of directors meet on January 15 to consider annual accounts for the financial year ended on June 30, 1996.
Hamid said the company had accumulated losses of 20 billion rupees, including seven billion suffered in 1995/96 (July-June).
